source: NCERT Class VII, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, Polity Ch. 1.

sections.heading: 1. Why We Need Government
points: A **government** makes rules, takes decisions and provides services for a society.
Governments differ in **who holds power** and **how leaders are chosen**.
Over history, societies have tried many **types of government**.

sections.heading: 2. Types of Government
points: **Monarchy** — rule by a **single person (king/queen)**, usually **hereditary**; power may be absolute or limited.
**Oligarchy** — rule by a **small group** of powerful people.
**Dictatorship** — rule by **one person/party** with total power, not chosen by the people.
**Democracy** — rule **by the people**, who choose their leaders through **elections**.
**Republic** — the head of state is **elected** (not a hereditary king).

sections.heading: 3. Direct and Representative Democracy
points: **Direct democracy** — people themselves take decisions in an assembly (possible only in small communities; e.g. ancient **ganas/sanghas**, the **Gram Sabha** today).
**Representative (indirect) democracy** — people **elect representatives** to govern on their behalf (used in large modern countries like India).
India is a **democratic republic** with representative democracy.

sections.heading: 4. From Rulers to the Ruled
points: Historically, most people were **subjects** ruled by kings, with **no say** in government.
The modern shift is from **subjects to citizens** — people who have **rights and a voice**.
In a democracy, **sovereignty rests with the people**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Monarchy = one hereditary ruler; oligarchy = small group; dictatorship = one person/party, total power.
Democracy = rule by the people (via elections); republic = elected head of state (no hereditary king).
Direct democracy = people decide directly (Gram Sabha, ancient sanghas); representative = elected reps.
India = a democratic republic with representative democracy.
Modern shift: from subjects to citizens; sovereignty with the people.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Republic** = **elected** head of state (not hereditary) — a country can be a democracy and a republic (like India).
**Direct democracy** works in **small** communities (Gram Sabha); large nations use **representative** democracy.
**Oligarchy** = rule by a **few**; **monarchy** = rule by **one** (usually hereditary).
In a democracy, ultimate power (**sovereignty**) lies with **the people**.
